report.summary: The repeated configured-boot crash is now addressed at the root and the change is verified in the built image — the event loop only enqueues into app_mqtt's own queue (all Wi-Fi/IP work on mqtt_net) and CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE reads 8192 in build/config/sdkconfig.h — but no configured boot has yet been observed succeeding; two new info notes (queue created under a conditional guard, sdkconfig.product precedence) and the standing spec deviations remain.

report.dataModel: No Matter/RainMaker model. MQTT: publish {"current_heating_setpoint": "<x.y>"} to zigbee2mqtt/<TRV> (qos1, retain 0); on connect subscribe every TRV/air-sensor topic and publish an empty message to each; {"time": 254} to zigbee2mqtt/bridge/request/permit_join; retained status zerocode/<mac12>/status with last-will. HTTP /settings (GET/POST), /api/state, /api/set.

app_mqtt_init (mqtt_net queue + task, handlers only enqueue, NVS config or compiled defaults, STA / onboarding AP)

app_display: one "Display setup started"; a duplicate init logs "app_display_init() called twice — ignored"

notes: CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE is 8192 in the generated header (build/config/sdkconfig.h:744) — the product's own event handler now only enqueues into an 8-deep queue, all Wi-Fi/IP work runs on mqtt_net.

The queue in app_mqtt is created only inside the `if (s_net_task == NULL)` block but its result is used unconditionally in the registration calls; on a hypothetical second app_mqtt_init after a failed task creation the handlers would be registered with NULL and silently drop events.

Standing behaviour notes from earlier rounds: plain-MQTT default broker, empty-payload poll to TRV state topics, single-button 10 s factory reset, three-number voice vocabulary (spec's 'set the office to 21' unsupported).
The configured boot has repeatedly failed (2304 and 4096); the 8192 build has not been booted yet.

peripherals.driver: app_audio (AFE + MultiNet) on app_dsp_shim's generic dot product
app_mqtt (queue-fed mqtt_net task, NVS config, STA / onboarding SoftAP, CA in NVS)

findings.description: The product's Wi-Fi/IP event path now depends on s_net_queue, but the queue is created inside the `if (s_net_task == NULL)` block while both esp_event_handler_register() calls pass s_net_queue unconditionally. On any path where the task creation is skipped or the queue was freed, the handlers are registered with NULL and silently drop every Wi-Fi/IP event, leaving the panel on the dashboard for ever with no retry and no log.
findings.evidence: app_mqtt.cpp:744-751 (queue + task created only when s_net_task == NULL, failure path sets s_net_task = NULL but leaves s_net_queue whatever it is); app_mqtt.cpp:753-754 registers both handlers with s_net_queue; app_mqtt.cpp:333-338 wifi_event_handler returns early when q == NULL.
findings.failureScenario: A second app_mqtt_init() call (or a retry after xTaskCreate failed) leaves s_net_task NULL and any stale/free queue behind: the handlers enqueue into nothing, STA_START is never handled, esp_wifi_connect() is never called, GOT_IP never arrives, and the LED shows 'connecting' for ever with no diagnostic. Today this needs two init calls, so it is latent rather than live.
findings.suggestedChange: Create the queue unconditionally (or outside the guard), check the queue before registering the handlers, and bail out with an error log if either is missing.

findings.description: The 8 KB default-loop stack only reaches the build through sdkconfig.product; the board layer still outranks sdkconfig.defaults, where the mandated CONFIG_EFUSE_VIRTUAL=y and the partition-table/flash-size pins live.
findings.evidence: firmware/sdkconfig.product (only CONFIG_ESP_SYSTEM_EVENT_TASK_STACK_SIZE=8192); firmware/build/config/sdkconfig.h:744 confirms 8192; the board manager reports board_manager.defaults has higher priority than sdkconfig.defaults (build log, report 047).
findings.failureScenario: A future edit that needs another board-overriding symbol puts it in sdkconfig.defaults and the board layer silently wins: the image keeps the board value and the fault the value was meant to prevent returns without any error.
findings.suggestedChange: Keep every board-overriding value in sdkconfig.product and check build/config/sdkconfig.h whenever one is added.
